reuse.why: Reuses linkBankSyncAccount and findOrCreateBank for the new provider, but the takeover clears the old account with a hand-copied field reset instead of reusing unlinkAccount's logic, and Fintegra download is a fresh copy of the Akahu function rather than a shared provider-parameterised one.

duplication.why: downloadFintegraTransactions is a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, linkFintegraAccount mirrors linkAkahuAccount, the replacedIds loop copies unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount block, and the assert call is pasted into all six provider handlers.

placement.why: Checks and linking live in accounts/app.ts and the download in accounts/sync.ts as the tree expects, but the guard runs in each provider handler instead of the shared linkBankSyncAccount path, and the closed-account rule is hidden inside a function named assertBankAccountNotLinked.

scope.why: Mostly focused on the four requests; the desktop-client edits are minimal and needed by the Record<BankSyncProviders, ...> types.

maintainability.why: Works through one helper, but the helper mixes two rules plus an override flag and returns ids to unlink, and every provider must remember to call it and thread replacedIds.

bypasses_abstraction.where: linkBankSyncAccount releases replaced accounts with its own db.updateAccount field reset instead of going through unlinkAccount (packages/loot-core/src/server/accounts/app.ts)

disguised_duplication.where: Copies (Fintegra download vs Akahu download, unlink field reset, provider link handler) are plain, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked gains the replaceExistingLink parameter and a closed-account branch unrelated to its name; linkBankSyncAccount gains replacedIds; the replace path re-implements unlinkAccount's reset instead of calling it.
